newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti denies Garuzzo's PC comments.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti denies Garuzzo's PC comments.

text.p: Italy's information technology group Olivetti denied on Thursday that its vice chairman Giorgio Garuzzo had made any comments regarding the planned sale of Olivetti's personal computer company.

Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore quoted Garuzzo saying the group "had received a better offer" for its PC company, after the paper said talks between Olivetti and corporate debt specialist Klesch & Co and U.S. financier Bennet Lebow had been frozen.

But an Olivetti spokesman said, "No press agency or press organisation, including Il Sole 24 Ore, has ever got in touch with nor collected any statement from Mr Garuzzo concerning on-going negotiations of the Olivetti group, including the one regarding Olivetti PCs".

Olivetti hopes to sell its loss-making PC company by the end of this year, but the group has consistently declined to make any comments on any potential talks with any prospective buyers until a deal is completed.
"No names, no comment until the deal is done," the Olivetti spokesman said.
Klesch said in September that it may have looked at various parts of Olivetti, but it declined to confirm that it was considering any type of bid.
The PC company has long been a thorn in the side of Olivetti, losing 200 billion lire ($132 million) in 1995, and some 15.8 billion in the first half of 1996.

Previous management at Olivetti had hoped to bring the company back to breakeven in 1996, but chief executive Roberto Colaninno, who took over in September, said the aim was to sell off the PC company by the end of the year.

Il Sole said the Olivetti talks were with Klesch and Lebow. These two groups had agreed to leave Bernard Auer as the head of PCs and maintain production and jobs at the PCs base at Scarmagno, near Ivrea in northwest Italy, the paper said.
In return, Olivetti's Systems and Services company would agree to buy around 50 percent of sales from the PC company, the paper added.

Olivetti shares surged to a day's high of 543 lire before ending up 5.72 percent at 537.8 lire on the Milan stock market where it was the most traded stock with nearly 48 million shares changing hands. ($1=1,516 lire)
